questions.question: Describe how the working drawing of the final stairs and ramp design is produced and which views and details it should include for a ramp that turns back on itself.
questions.expected_answer: It follows the method from earlier in the term: choose views and a scale such as 1:50, convert sizes in a table, set out the front view, project the plan below and the end view on the opposite side, add hidden detail, correct line types, dimension each size once in real millimetres and complete the title block with scale, first angle symbol and units. For a turning ramp the plan is the most informative view, showing both legs, the turning landing, stairs, door swing and site boundary; the elevation shows the step profile, rise per leg and rail heights; a section on a chain line through the ramp shows slab thickness, fill, kerb and rail post fixing.

questions.question: Explain how the working drawing is checked against the specifications and what is done if a specification is not met.
questions.expected_answer: Each specification is checked against a dimension on the drawing and recorded: ramp length per leg divided by rise gives 12 or more; width 1 200 or more; riser times count equals 600 with all risers equal; treads 250 or more; rails on both sides at 900 to 1 000 extending 300; landings 1 200 or more at top, bottom and turn, the top clear of the door swing arc; kerb 75 in section; a non-slip finish note; overall size within the site. A failure is corrected on the drawing, for example lengthening a leg, never excused. The drawing is also checked for alignment of views, single dimensions and distinct line weights.

questions.question: Draw or describe a flow chart for making the model, naming the symbols and explaining where the decision checks are placed and why.
questions.expected_answer: Symbols: oval for start and end, rectangle for an action, diamond for a yes or no decision with two labelled arrows, arrows for order. Sequence: start; gather materials and tools; convert drawing sizes to model scale 1:20; mark out the base; cut ramp legs and landing; check gradient, no returns to recut; assemble ramp; cut four steps; check risers equal; assemble stairs; fit kerb; cut and fit posts at scaled 900; check rail height; fit handrails both sides; texture and paint; final check against specifications; end. Checks are placed after cutting and before gluing, where errors are cheap to fix, and before irreversible steps such as painting.
